html:
In December 1787 men of the French expedition of La Pérouse were attacked while taking on water at Aʻasu on Tutuila. Twelve of them were killed, including the captain Fleuriot de Langle. The bay is still called Massacre Bay.

La Pérouse was exploring the Pacific in the wake of James Cook. After Tutuila he sailed to Australia, then vanished; his ships were later found wrecked at Vanikoro in the Solomon Islands.

Reports of the clash gave Samoa a fierce name in Europe. Few ships called there until missionaries of the London Missionary Society arrived in 1830.
